correctness.rationale: For recomputed distances after at most q deletions, the union of the faulty lines has at most q(q+1)<N points. A point outside that union has an intact joining line to every other point. Dually there is a line avoiding all faulty point pencils. Positive retained degrees then give connectivity and the clean point has distance at most three to every vertex. In the radius-two flag complex a mixed clique cannot have two vertices in each shore, by absence of four-cycles. The two pieces of cliques with at most one vertex of one shore intersect in precisely the retained graph. Each collapses to its pure-shore complex by removing a simplex attached along its nonempty neighbor face, separately for each exceptional vertex; the pure-shore complexes are cones on the clean witnesses. The cofibration pushout gives the suspension of the retained graph, whose cycle rank is (q+1)N-t-2N+1=q^3-t. Radius one is that graph and radius three onward is a cone; integral distances give the stated half-open bars. For nested faults the Mayer–Vietoris connecting maps to the graph cycle groups are natural. A spanning tree of the smaller graph works in both graphs, so the smaller fundamental cycle basis is a subset of the larger one; the free cokernel has exactly |F'|-|F| generators. The simplicial cofiber is simply connected by van Kampen and has just that reduced H2 by the relative sequence; Hurewicz plus the simply connected homology Whitehead theorem gives the wedge. Deleting all q+1 incidences at a point defeats uniform connectivity. This is an analytic check of RESULT.md lines 18–30. The frozen Python verifier was inspected but not run; its exact binary homology samples in prime orders are supplementary, not an integral certificate or an all-order proof.

evidence: Chachólski et al. Theorems 8.6 and 12.5 give general homotopy-fiber/gluing criteria with obstruction-complex and simplex hypotheses; Adams–Coskunuzer place Rips of graphs in the power filtration and discuss bounds. Neither inspected passage asserts arbitrary projective-plane incidence-edge stability.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General decomposition machinery does not supply the two simultaneous clean witnesses after arbitrary faults. Those witnesses and the separate relative comparison are the specific inputs necessary to infer the theorem.

evidence: The star-fault proof is explicitly restricted to one star. The intact suspension proof and general gluing theory give reusable methods, not an assertion that the shores of every scattered-fault graph are contractible.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The step from a clean undeleted plane or fixed star to arbitrary placement requires the simultaneous projective-plane covering count, with no transitivity assumption. Once established, the homotopy and primitive lattice conclusions use standard tools; these tools are not themselves originality claims.

evidence: The intact paper has exactly the t=0 filtration. The one-star record states q^3-t spheres and primitive split maps up to t=q at a single point. The vertex-deletion record has q^3-q spheres and a primitive map with cokernel Z^q.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Point-line duality also covers the one-line star, but does not turn scattered faults into one star. Removing a whole vertex is not retaining it with at least one incident edge; equal generator counts at particular t do not identify the filtrations or comparison maps.

evidence: The Fano catalogue record gives rank 8-t up to two faults and examples of different ranks at three faults when connected. The submitted checks enumerate low-order patterns and sample binary homology.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Credit the exact q=2 Betti overlap. Three faults at q=2 lie outside the certified budget. Neither a prime-order sample nor the Fano rank result determines the all-plane integral homotopy types and nested maps.

originality.rationale: Credit the intact classification and suspension construction, the primitive single-vertex deletion result, and in particular the full one-star overlap. The supported distinct claim is the same sharp radius-two stability for every placement of up to q deleted incidences with recomputed distances, together with the arbitrary nested-fault comparison/cofiber. The closest catalogue record is dated the same day and is not discarded on that account; its explicit star hypothesis prevents full coverage. This is a best-of-knowledge comparison, not a priority claim.
residual_risks: The Parks–Marchette full text was not obtained; no conclusion about its entire coverage is inferred.
No publication ordering is inferred for the two records dated 2026-11-22; other unindexed generalizations may exist.

value.rationale: Fault tolerance of the graph-metric filtration is a natural structural question because every deleted edge can change distances, not just remove itself. One simultaneous witness argument handles all layouts and all existing planes, reaches the sharp uniform budget, and controls primitive maps and cofibers rather than just equal field Betti counts.
